newsitem.title: USA: Wis. fiscal bureau ups revenue forecast $230 mln.
newsitem.headline: Wis. fiscal bureau ups revenue forecast $230 mln.

text.p: The Wisconsin Legislative Fiscal Bureau has increased its tax revenue estimates $230 million for the current fiscal year and upcoming fiscal biennium.

The bureau increased its revenue forecast $210 million for individual income taxes, $15 million for corporate taxes and $5 million for estate taxes, Director Robert Lang said in a letter to legislative leaders earlier this week.

The bureau had estimated in January that income tax collections would grow by 6.7 percent in the current fiscal year over the previous year, but growth as of April was "significantly greater," Lang wrote.
The May forecast for the U.S. economy has improved somewhat over the forecast used for the January estimates as well, Lang wrote.

Corporate income tax and franchise tax collections are also expected to increase, based on stronger than anticipated collections through April and an expected increase in corporate profits in 1997, Lang wrote.
The estate tax estimate increased $5 million based on unexpected one-time receipts in April and May, Lang found.
Sales tax projections remained unchanged and collections from other state taxes were generally consistent with the January projections, Lang found.
State Sen. Brian Burke, D-Milwaukee, believes the extra revenue should be used to cut property taxes. Burke is Senate chair of the joint legislative finance committee now reviewing the budget.
The joint finance committee hopes to complete its line-by-line review by the end of May, said Burke's spokesman, Bob Allen. The Wisconsin fiscal biennium begins on July 1.
